historicalDate.original: Bounded continuity of the verified 1987–1989 USSR legal-border state until formal Union recognition of Baltic independence on 6 September 1991

baseStates.notes: Bounded legal-border continuity only. Lithuania's March 1990 declaration and the 1990–1991 Baltic restoration acts are not silently treated as Union-recognized external-border changes. The state stops before September 1991, when the USSR State Council formally recognized the independence of Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia. September–December 1991 therefore require a distinct geometry excluding the Baltic republics.
